contract.reader: An engineering student or engineer comfortable with basic circuit analysis, calculus and elementary statistics, deciding whether and where to start the series
contract.problem: Knowing what the seven entries cover, why in this order, which examples connect them and which conventions they share
contract.outcome: Follow the measurement chain that orders the series; know the two running examples (PT100, load-cell channel), the units, the VIM/GUM vocabulary and noise conventions; have five checkable objectives
contract.contribution: The order is the measurement chain of the first entry, and two running examples are traced entry by entry
contract.evidence: The seven entries; the running-example and convention statements were checked against them in the live review
contract.limitations: An overview; total reading time not stated; entry 6 is the subject of no objective

findings.location: Entries list, cards 1 to 7 (desktop-light-02 to 04; mobile-light-04 to 07)
findings.problem: All seven entry descriptions are verbless fragments, six ending in topic lists, not one sentence saying what the reader will learn
findings.whyItMatters: Standards 8.1; on the front door the cards read as tables of contents, and the same text is each entry's meta description and RSS summary
findings.action: Rewrite the seven entry descriptions as one sentence each (70-165 characters) through each entry's review stages, with the Vietnamese descriptions in the same commit
findings.acceptance: Every entry card shows a one-sentence description of what the reader will learn and none is a section list

history.note: live review: accepted-with-follow-up (editorial/live-reviews/series/sensor-systems.md); library decision: retain
